README.html.title: GraphQL-Markdown + DocFX demo | GraphQL Documentation with Docfx
README.html.summary: GraphQL-Markdown + DocFX demo This project demonstrates how to generate GraphQL documentation with GraphQL-Markdown for a DocFX site using the modern template. Live demo: graphql-markdown.dev/demo-docfx Quick start npm install npm run dev Open http://localhost:8080/ and browse the GraphQL API section in the left navigation. Prerequisites Node.js 20 or later .NET SDK 8 or later DocFX installed as a global .NET tool: dotnet tool install -g docfx Commands Command Action npm install Install dependencies npm run generate Generate docs from the GraphQL schema npm run dev Generate docs + serve a local DocFX preview npm run build Generate docs + build a static site to _site/ npm run test:visual Run Playwright + Argos visual tests against _site/ (build first) npm run clean Remove generated files and build output Project structure . ├── content/ │ └── index.md # Homepage source for the GraphQL API section ├── docs/ │ ├── graphql/ # Generated GraphQL documentation │ │ ├── index.md # GraphQL API overview (copied from content/index.md) │ │ ├── toc.yml # Generated navigation │ │ ├── operations/ # Queries, mutations, subscriptions │ │ └── types/ # Objects, scalars, directives │ ├── introduction.md │ ├── getting-started.md │ └── toc.yml ├── scripts/ │ ├── custom-docfx-mdx.mjs # Custom MDX formatter (badge colors, page H1 title) │ └── generate-docs.mjs # GraphQL-Markdown runner ├── template/public/ # DocFX modern template overrides │ ├── main.css # Styles for generated GraphQL pages (light/dark) │ └── main.js # Points field names at their heading anchors ├── tests/visual/ # Playwright + Argos screenshot tests ├── docfx.json # DocFX site configuration ├── index.md # Landing page (raw HTML, styled by main.css) ├── toc.yml # Top-level navigation └── package.json Notes The documented schema is the shared GraphQL-Markdown demo schema used by all GraphQL-Markdown demos, loaded from its raw URL at generation time. The preset @graphql-markdown/formatters/docfx provides: DocFX alert syntax (> [!NOTE], > [!WARNING], etc.) for admonitions Bootstrap 5 badge classes (badge text-bg-{variant}) for type badges Path-derived uid front matter for unique DocFX cross-reference targets (e.g. operations-queries-projects) afterRenderTypeEntitiesHook that builds toc.yml navigation files at every directory level automatically Badge colors can be customized in scripts/custom-docfx-mdx.mjs by spreading BADGE_CLASS_MAP and overriding individual entries. template/public/main.css restyles the formatter output (entity chips, pill badges, field rows, code blocks, alerts) using Bootstrap theme variables, so it follows DocFX's light/dark switch. toc.yml files in docs/graphql/ are generated at doc-generation time and should not be edited manually.

docs/getting-started.html.title: Getting Started | GraphQL Documentation with Docfx
docs/getting-started.html.summary: Getting Started Prerequisites Node.js 20 or later .NET SDK 8 or later DocFX installed as a global .NET tool: dotnet tool install -g docfx Install dependencies npm install Generate the GraphQL docs npm run generate This runs graphql-markdown against the shared demo schema (loaded from its URL) and writes Markdown pages to docs/graphql/. It also builds the DocFX toc.yml navigation files for each section via the custom formatter hook. Serve locally npm run dev This generates the docs then starts a DocFX local server at http://localhost:8080. Build static site npm run build The built site is written to _site/.

docs/graphql/index.html.title: GraphQL API Reference | GraphQL Documentation with Docfx
docs/graphql/index.html.summary: GraphQL API Reference This section contains the auto-generated API reference for the shared GraphQL-Markdown demo schema, produced by graphql-markdown using the DocFX formatter. Schema overview The demo API models a small project workspace: Queries — list folders and projects, and search across them Mutations — create folders and projects, archive projects Subscriptions — follow project changes and new folders Types — Folder, Project, User (all implementing Node), the SearchResult union, enums, inputs and custom directives Usage Browse the sections in the left navigation to explore available queries and types.

docs/graphql/operations/queries/folders..title: folders | GraphQL Documentation with Docfx
docs/graphql/operations/queries/folders..summary: folders List folders available in the current workspace. folders( limit: Int offset: Int ): [Folder!]! Arguments folders.limit ● Int scalar Maximum number of folders to return. folders.offset ● Int scalar Number of folders to skip before returning results. docs/graphql/operations/queries/projects.title: projects | GraphQL Documentation with Docfx
docs/graphql/operations/queries/projects.summary: projects List projects, optionally filtered by lifecycle status. projects( status: ProjectStatus limit: Int ): ProjectConnection! Arguments projects.status ● ProjectStatus enum Limit results to projects in this lifecycle stage. projects.limit ● Int scalar Maximum number of projects to return. Defaults to 20. Type ProjectConnection object A paginated project result set. Example query ListActiveProjects($status: ProjectStatus) { projects(status: $status) { totalCount nodes { id name status owner { name } } } }

docs/graphql/operations/queries/search.h.title: search | GraphQL Documentation with Docfx
docs/graphql/operations/queries/search.h.summary: search Search folders, projects, and users from a single endpoint. search( query: String! ): [SearchResult!]! Arguments search.query ● String! non-null scalar Text matched against folder, project, and user names. Type SearchResult union A result returned from global workspace search. Example query SearchWorkspace($query: String!) { search(query: $query) { __typename ... on Folder { id name } ... on Project { id name status } ... on User { id name email } } }

docs/graphql/operations/subscriptions/fo.title: folderCreated | GraphQL Documentation with Docfx

docs/graphql/operations/subscriptions/pr.title: projectChanged | GraphQL Documentation with Docfx
docs/graphql/operations/subscriptions/pr.summary: projectChanged Receive an event whenever a project changes in the workspace. projectChanged( projectId: ID types: [ProjectEventType!] ): ProjectEvent! Arguments projectChanged.projectId ● ID scalar Limit events to a single project. projectChanged.types ● [ProjectEventType!] list enum Limit events to these change kinds. Type ProjectEvent object A change delivered to subscribers watching a project. Example subscription WatchProject($projectId: ID, $types: [ProjectEventType!]) { projectChanged(projectId: $projectId, types: $types) { type occurredAt project { id name status } actor { name } } }

docs/introduction.html.title: Introduction | GraphQL Documentation with Docfx
docs/introduction.html.summary: Introduction This demo shows how to use graphql-markdown with the DocFX formatter to generate API reference documentation from a GraphQL schema. How it works graphql-markdown introspects a GraphQL schema and generates Markdown pages for every query, mutation, type, input, enum, scalar, and directive. The DocFX formatter (@graphql-markdown/formatters/docfx) adapts the output for DocFX: Injects a uid field in YAML front matter for cross-reference resolution Uses DocFX alert syntax (> [!NOTE], > [!WARNING], etc.) for admonitions Renders badges as Bootstrap <span class="badge"> elements, styled as pills by the demo template Schema The demo uses the shared GraphQL-Markdown demo schema, the same small project-workspace API documented by every GraphQL-Markdown demo. It is loaded from its raw URL at generation time. Source See Getting Started to run the demo locally.
